summary_for_children: Al-'Alaq means The Clinging Substance. Its first ayahs were the first revelation: Recite in the name of your Lord who created, who taught by the pen.
world_title: Recite! The Pen and the Clinging Substance
environment_concept: A rocky hill rises over the path with a small cave high on its side. The surah does not describe this place; the cave follows the hadith of the first revelation and is labelled as such. Below, a writing desk holds a reed pen, ink and blank paper (96:4), and a quiet terrace invites prostration (96:19). No person is shown.
architecture_and_scenery: A steep hill with a cave mouth, a writing desk with reed pen, inkwell and paper, a prayer terrace.

areas.name: Hill of Revelation
areas.description: A high hill with a small cave. The surah does not describe the place; the cave follows the hadith of the first revelation.

areas.name: The Pen

areas.name: Draw Near
areas.description: A clean, quiet terrace for prayer.

narration_plan: The Prophet (peace be upon him) and the angel are never shown or voiced.
required_assets: Writing desk, reed pen and ink

status.playable_environment: first version built: its own scene (a hill with a cave, a writing desk with a reed pen and a prayer terrace) and two playable games
status.testing: checked in headless Chromium with software WebGL at 1280x800; not tested on phones or real GPUs
status.tested_by: automated screenshots of the scene and the games

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: A village school courtyard in the morning with a writing bench under a fig tree, reed beds by a stream and an ink pot

primary_mechanic.text: Cut a reed pen (a flat cut is refused; the tip must be cut at a slant and split), then trace four practice stroke shapes dot by dot in stroke order; the reed carries ink for only three dots, so tapping dry is refused and dipping a wet reed is refused. Practice shapes only: no Quran text is drawn.

unique_world.narrative_structure: A reading on the path, cutting the pen and practising letters, then a reading by the school wall
environment_behaviour: each practice sheet turns from blank to written
unique_world.learning_objective: Know that Allah taught by the pen what man did not know (96:4-5)

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: Read!
story_library.children_narration: The opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq call us to read in the name of the Lord who created. They remind us that Allah teaches human beings what they did not know. Learning is a wonderful gift, but knowledge should lead us toward humility rather than arrogance.

world_idea.title: The Cave of Learning
world_idea.description: Explore a quiet cave-inspired environment and an interactive learning workshop featuring letters, language, and discovery. The context of the first revelation is presented through sourced narration, without depicting Prophet Muhammad or Jibril.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The cave of Hira and Jibril are not shown. The context of the first revelation comes from hadith and is labelled as hadith, not Quran.
